title: Constant module restriction with commutative coefficient transport
statement: Let C be a category with objects in universe u and morphisms in v, J a Grothendieck topology, R a commutative ring in max(u,v), and U an object. Restrict modules over the constant commutative ring sheaf to C/U, then restrict scalars along the canonical constantSheafOverIso from constant R on C/U to the restricted constant R sheaf. This functor, commutativeConstantSliceRestriction, is additive and exact. Constant realization [def-sfb-site-derived-constant-module-functor] followed by this functor is naturally isomorphic to constant realization on C/U.

source.place: Remark 3.2, restriction of constants; Stacks Modules on Sites Sections 03CY and 03DH

proof.text: The source constantSheafOverIso carries the slice sheafification unit of each scalar r to the restricted original unit. Apply this identity to show that the restricted module sheafification unit is linear after the specified coefficient transport.

The module sheafification Hom equivalence extends that linear presheaf map to a module sheaf map. Its underlying sheaf map composed with the slice unit is the restricted original unit. Restricted original units are locally bijective since slice coverings are underlying coverings. Cancel the slice unit in the local-injectivity and local-surjectivity criteria to prove the map is an isomorphism.

Precompose the naturality square with the slice sheafification unit. The factorization formula reduces it to naturality of the original unit, which proves the claimed natural isomorphism. Exactness follows from exact slice restriction and exact scalar restriction.
